# Introduction

This document generates line plots to show individual variability in Mtb_Ag-induced cytokine
responses during successful treatment (Figure S9). Each line represents one
patient tracked across visits. Lines are coloured red for patients infected with
Mtb lineage 2 whose concentration exceeds their Visit 0 value at any subsequent
visit, blue for lineage 4 patients with the same pattern, and black for patients
whose concentration does not exceed their Visit 0 value.

# Load packages

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(readxl)
library(DataExplorer)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Define file paths

```{r}
input_file    <- "Input/Cytokines_cleaned_log10_Predict-TB.xlsx"
lineage_file  <- "Input/Demographic and clinical information.xlsx"
output_s9     <- "Output/Figure_S9"

dir.create(output_s9, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Load data

```{r}
all_data <- read_excel(input_file, sheet = 1)

head(all_data)
dim(all_data)
```

# Load lineage data

The lineage file is loaded and reduced to the two columns needed for joining.
Check that the patient ID column name matches ID1 used in the protein data.

```{r}
lineage_data <- read_excel(lineage_file, sheet = 1) %>%
  select(ID1, main_lineage) %>%
  distinct()

head(lineage_data)
cat(sprintf(
  "Patients with lineage data: %d | Lineages present: %s\n",
  nrow(lineage_data),
  paste(unique(lineage_data$main_lineage), collapse = ", ")
))
```

# Filter to successful treatment outcome and Mtb_Ag stimulation

```{r}
protein_data <- all_data %>%
  filter(Comments == "success") %>%
  filter(Condition == "Mtb_Ag")
```

# Define cytokine columns

```{r}
cytokine_cols <- c(
  "BDNF", "CCL11", "Factor_VII", "ICAM_1",
  "IL_1_alpha", "IL_1_beta", "IL_10", "IL_12p40",
  "IL_12p70", "IL_18", "IL_1RA", "IL_3", "IL_4",
  "IL_6", "IL_7", "IL_8", "CCL2", "CCL3",
  "MMP_3", "TNF", "VEGF", "IFNG", "IL_2",
  "pan_IFNA", "IFNB"
)
```

# Line plot function

For each cytokine, patients are flagged as increased if their concentration
exceeds their Visit 0 value at any subsequent visit. Increased patients are
then coloured by Mtb lineage: red for lineage 2 and blue for lineage 4.
Patients without an increase are shown in black. Patients with no Visit 0
measurement or no lineage information are shown in black.

```{r}
plot_cytokine_lines <- function(data,
                                cytokine_name,
                                lineage_data = NULL,
                                save_path    = NULL,
                                plot_width   = 4,
                                plot_height  = 6.5) {

  plot_data <- data %>%
    select(ID1, Visit, Condition, Concentration = all_of(cytokine_name)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Concentration)) %>%
    mutate(Visit = as.numeric(Visit))

  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    warning(paste("No data for", cytokine_name))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  # Visit 0 baseline per patient and condition
  baseline <- plot_data %>%
    filter(Visit == 0) %>%
    select(ID1, Condition, Baseline = Concentration)

  # Flag patients where concentration exceeds baseline at any post-baseline visit
  plot_data <- plot_data %>%
    left_join(baseline, by = c("ID1", "Condition")) %>%
    group_by(ID1, Condition) %>%
    mutate(
      increased = any(Concentration[Visit != 0] > Baseline, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

  # Join lineage information if provided
  if (!is.null(lineage_data)) {
    plot_data <- plot_data %>%
      left_join(lineage_data, by = "ID1")
  } else {
    plot_data <- plot_data %>%
      mutate(main_lineage = NA_character_)
  }

  # Assign line colour based on increased status and lineage
  plot_data <- plot_data %>%
    mutate(
      line_color = case_when(
        !increased                        ~ "Not increased",
        increased & main_lineage == "lineage2" ~ "Lineage 2",
        increased & main_lineage == "lineage4" ~ "Lineage 4",
        TRUE                              ~ "Not increased"
      )
    )

  visit_range <- range(plot_data$Visit, na.rm = TRUE)

  p <- ggplot(
      plot_data,
      aes(x = Visit, y = Concentration, group = ID1, color = line_color)
    ) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(size = 1) +
    facet_grid(~ Condition) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = seq(visit_range[1], visit_range[2], by = 8)
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(
        "Lineage 2"    = "red",
        "Lineage 4"    = "#00CCFF",
        "Not increased" = "black"
      ),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    labs(
      title = cytokine_name,
      x     = "Visit (Week)",
      y     = "Concentration (log10 pg/mL)"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.border     = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = "black"),
      legend.position  = "bottom"
    )

  print(p)

  if (!is.null(save_path)) {
    ggsave(
      filename = file.path(save_path, paste0(cytokine_name, "_lines.png")),
      plot     = p,
      width    = plot_width,
      height   = plot_height,
      units    = "in"
    )
  }

  invisible(p)
}
```

# Figure S9: Line plots across all conditions

```{r}
for (cyt in cytokine_cols) {
  plot_cytokine_lines(
    data          = protein_data,
    cytokine_name = cyt,
    lineage_data  = lineage_data,
    save_path     = output_s9
  )
}
```

# Patient lookup table

A subset of cytokines measured under Mtb_Ag stimulation is extracted to help
identify patients with distinct response patterns.

```{r}
lookup_cytokines <- c("IFNG", "IL_1RA", "IL_1_beta", "IL_2")

patient_lookup <- protein_data %>%
  select(ID1, Visit, Condition, all_of(lookup_cytokines)) %>%
  filter(Condition == "Mtb_Ag") %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(lookup_cytokines), ~ .x)) %>%
  left_join(lineage_data, by = "ID1")

head(patient_lookup)
```
